chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, client of the Children of Hashim, narrated to us. He said: al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Sulayman from 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi. He said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), when a man from the people of Tus entered upon him. He said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! What is [the reward] for one who visits the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)? So he said to him: O Tusi! Whoever visits the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), while knowing that he is an Imam from God whose obedience is obligatory upon the servants — God will forgive him his past and future sins, and will accept his intercession for seventy sinners, and he will not ask God, Mighty and Majestic, for any need at his grave except that He will fulfill it for him.

He said: Then Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) entered, so [Imam Sadiq] seated him on his lap and began to kiss his forehead, then turned to him [the Tusi man] and said: O Tusi! Indeed he is the Imam, the Caliph, and the Proof after me. And from his loins will come forth a man who will be pleasing to God, Mighty and Majestic, in His heavens, and to His servants on His earth. He will be killed in your land by poison, in oppression and hostility, and will be buried there as a stranger. Verily, whoever visits him in his solitude — while knowing that he is an Imam after his father, whose obedience is obligatory from God, Mighty and Majestic — shall be as one who visited the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family and peace).

key_terms.الحجة: The Proof/Hujja — a title for the Imam as God's authoritative representative and proof to humanity
key_terms.رضا: Rida — both a description (he who is pleasing to God) and an allusion to the title/name of the eighth Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida
key_terms.غربته: His solitude/estrangement — referring to the spiritual and geographical isolation of the buried Imam Rida in Tus, far from his homeland
key_terms.مفترض الطاعة: One whose obedience is divinely obligatory — a technical term in Shia theology for the divinely appointed Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn, according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a gathering with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) where a man from Tus inquired about the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (AS). The Imam declared that visiting Imam Husayn's grave with faith in his divine Imamate brings complete forgiveness and the acceptance of one's intercession for seventy sinners. The hadith then recounts a remarkable moment: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) entered as a child and Imam Sadiq declared him the next Imam, and prophesied that from his loins would come a man (Imam Rida) who would be martyred in Khurasan and buried as a stranger — making his visitation equivalent to visiting the Prophet (SAWW). The audience for this hadith — a man from Tus (in Khurasan) — receives a direct prophecy about the future significance of his homeland.
